expect:
Students may include (Holderness or Medmerry):
• Hard engineering: Mappleton sea wall and rock groynes (1991, £2 million) protect 50 cliff-top properties — sea wall and groynes block erosion but interrupt sediment supply, accelerating loss of land at Cowden and Aldbrough downdrift.
• Soft engineering: Bournemouth beach replenishment costs around £3 million per kilometre every 5 years but absorbs wave energy and supports tourism — must be repeated, sediment supply may be limited.
• Sustainable approaches: Medmerry Managed Realignment (2013) breached the sea wall, flooded 183 hectares of farmland, now protects 348 homes and is an RSPB reserve — saves money and creates habitat, but loses farmland and is unpopular with displaced landowners.
• Conflict: residents of Happisburgh wanted defences but were refused on cost-benefit grounds.
• Conclusion: a mix of approaches, coordinated through Integrated Coastal Zone Management, is increasingly seen as the best way to balance protection, environment and cost.
Mastering (7–8): all three approaches with named examples and clear evaluation.
Secure (5–6): two approaches with examples.
Developing (3–4): one approach covered well.
Emerging (1–2): vague description with no examples.

expect:
Examine how globalisation and free-trade policies have changed the UK economy. Refer to TNCs and FDI in your answer.
(8 marks plus 4 SPaG)

Assess the impact of globalisation and free-trade policies on the UK economy. Refer to TNCs and FDI in your answer.
(8 marks plus 4 SPaG)
note: F17: wrong command word for this board.

expect:
Students may include:
• Free-trade policies and privatisation since 1980s opened the UK to foreign investment.
• TNCs have brought jobs and technology — Nissan in Sunderland (employing around 6,000), JLR's Indian Tata Motors ownership, Toyota at Burnaston.
• FDI has averaged £100bn/year, making the UK one of the world's largest investment destinations.
• Risks: profits return overseas; sudden withdrawal can devastate communities (Honda Swindon closure 2019, Tata Steel reductions in Port Talbot 2024).
• Decline of older industries — UK shed steel, mining and shipbuilding jobs as cheaper foreign producers competed (Consett 1980, Wearside shipyards by 1988).
• Mixed regional outcomes — South East thrived from finance and services, the North East and Wales lost industries; new investment is uneven.
• Conclusion: globalisation has on balance grown the UK economy, but spread the gains unevenly.
Mastering (7–8): balanced view with named TNCs/FDI examples and judgement.
Secure (5–6): mainly one-sided with examples.
Developing (3–4): vague generalisations with one example.
Emerging (1–2): minimal.
